Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray shows prominent, tortuous vascular markings in the right lower zone without a distinct mass or consolidation, which is characteristic of systemic arterialization (often from an aberrant systemic artery) supplying the lung and causing hemoptysis. This finding distinguishes it from intralobar sequestration (which typically presents as consolidation), AVMs (which show discrete nodules with feeding/draining vessels), or normal variants.
